_purpose: PCI DSS 6.4.3(c) requires a written inventory of every script on the payment page, each with a justification. The prose inventory lives beside the prod CSP it describes, at OBRS-backend/deploy/prod/PAYMENT-PAGE-SCRIPT-INVENTORY.md. THIS file is the machine-readable half of it for the surfaces only this repo can change, and scripts/check-payment-page-scripts.mjs enforces it. Edit both together.
_note: The two repos each gate what they can break: this file vs the frontend's scripts and netlify.toml, and CspAllowlistMatchesInventoryTest vs the prod Caddyfile. Neither can read the other's tree, so the prose document is the seam - keep the origin lists in the two files in step by hand when the policy changes.
_origins_note: OBRS-882: `origins` is an ARRAY because one file can load from more than one vendor, and the single-string `origin` it replaced could not say so - a loader's SECOND vendor satisfied the old rule 4 while appearing in no inventory and no CSP. check-payment-page-scripts.mjs now compares this list against the https origins the file actually names, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

scriptLoaders.why: Required to take card payments at all. omise.js defines both window.Omise and window.OmiseCard; OmiseCard renders the card fields inside an iframe on cdn.omise.co and posts a token back, which is what keeps the PAN off this origin (OBRS-391). Removing it would mean collecting the PAN ourselves.

Google Identity Services - the 'Sign in with Google' button. Loaded from TypeScript rather than index.html specifically so it stays OFF the payment page (OBRS-719 AC 3). The hl locale must be a query param on the script URL; GIS exposes no initialize() option for it (OBRS-90).
Google Maps JS for the home-page route map. NOT a payment-page script - listed because maps.googleapis.com is in the site-wide script-src and a single CSP header cannot be route-scoped.

GA4 (gtag.js) and Microsoft Clarity, added by OBRS-867 to answer where customers drop out of the booking funnel - OBRS-862 and OBRS-872 are both blocked on that. STATE IT PLAINLY: AnalyticsService.init() runs in the app shell and AnalyticsTagsService.load() fires on the consent stream, so once a customer accepts, BOTH tags are on EVERY route INCLUDING /payment. These are payment-page scripts. What makes that acceptable is the same argument as for the rest of this page: card fields live in an iframe on cdn.omise.co, so same-origin policy denies these scripts - and anything injected into them - any access to the PAN (OBRS-391). Two further limits are load-bearing rather than incidental: nothing is injected until AnalyticsConsentService reports 'granted' (a PDPA requirement that doubles as a smaller attack surface), and an empty ID is a total no-op, so CI and every fresh clone run with no third-party script at all. What this does NOT buy is integrity of the bytes those two origins serve - see section 3 of the prose inventory; the residual is accepted on the same terms as Omise's and Google's.
